analysis: Examined LaunchAgent.swift (head text) and the WaitHonestChecks.swift test patch. The only production change is in LaunchAgent.swift: two entries (GenerationLoopGuardPolicy.environmentKey, GenerationLoopExitThinkingPolicy.environmentKey) were added to the inferencePassthroughEnvKeys allowlist (lines 454-455), plus a doc comment (421-423). passthroughEnvironment (lines 486-513) forwards only non-empty allowlisted values into the launchd plist's EnvironmentVariables. The two new keys are operator-set tuning/rollback knobs for a Gemma 4 loop guard, i.e. a generation-behaviour toggle. They do not touch keys, attestation, the prompt/ciphertext paths, the prefix cache (T-041) or the App Attest worker opt-in. The worker key is still restricted to the exact value "1", and fault flags are still excluded (lines 500-504). The values are written to a plist in the user-owned ~/Library/LaunchAgents. That is an existing same-user trust surface (TB-003), and nothing here widens it. A local operator who can edit the plist already controls the provider, so the change adds no new capability. Residual question: the loop guard accepts a list of model_types, and the parsing of that value lives outside the supplied evidence. I did not see how the parser handles malformed input, so it is unverified, but nothing suggests a security impact. The WaitHonestChecks.swift change is test-only: it adds cluster onboarding stop-detection checks (a stop is the leader's stop-count record, not its status words). It is non-shipping, with no security-relevant production code and no secrets. The production implementations those tests exercise (ClusterOnboardingStopped, ClusterOnboardingFollowedStop) are outside the supplied units, so their correctness is unreviewed. No regressions or new attack surface were identified in the supplied units.
